## Trial `alias-based-policy-ubuntu24__aq9RmKJ`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** All material outcomes of the task were satisfied with direct evidence: node1 routes between lan-a and lan-b with forwarding confirmed, a single named port alias (node3_svc_ports) was created for 8080/8443/9000 and referenced by exactly one firewall rule that pf correctly expands into per-port pass entries, node2's reachability to node3 on the three ports (and denial of an unlisted port and reverse traffic) was proven with real payload delivery, and the mandatory node-restart protocol was executed on all three nodes with distinct pre/post boot identities and full recovery of networking, firewall, and connectivity state re-verified after each restart.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.880 | 0.920 | 48/2 (+6 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **req-1 — Satisfied:** node1 routes between lan-a and lan-b (topology + IP forwarding)
  - **Why:** OPT1 (vtnet1, 10.60.1.1/24) and OPT2 (vtnet2, 10.60.2.1/24) interfaces were added to node1's config.xml and applied via rc.reload_all ('Configuring LAN_A interface...done'/'Configuring LAN_B interface...done'). Post-apply ifconfig confirms both addresses live and net.inet.ip.forwarding=1. node2 and node3 were statically addressed with routes through node1 and end-to-end TCP traffic across the router was later verified working, confirming actual routing (not just configuration).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-15219ac0cecd4238`, `cmd-95b55f2c23104b2c`, `cmd-8785934171b744db`, `cmd-1b1658bf79534866`, `cmd-9042fdfda5114f6a`, `cmd-66d5df9eeca54810`
- **req-2 — Satisfied:** Ports 8080, 8443, 9000 expressed as a single named alias object on node1, referenced by the rule instead of one rule per port
  - **Why:** A single OPNsense port alias 'node3_svc_ports' (content 8080/8443/9000) was created, and exactly one filter rule was added whose destination port field references that alias name rather than an individual port. After configctl filter reload, pfctl -sr shows pf expanding the single alias-referencing rule into three underlying pass lines (http-alt/8443/9000) sharing the same rule label, which is the expected pf behavior for an alias and confirms the rule was authored against the alias, not duplicated manually.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-b15944886e42428f`, `cmd-3c90a8813e27443c`, `cmd-61bac14744704480`, `cmd-69e5c406885b4a18`
- **req-3 — Satisfied:** node2 can reach node3 on TCP 8080, 8443, 9000; unrelated traffic remains denied
  - **Why:** With listeners on node3 for 8080/8443/9000 (plus 2222 as a negative control), node2 successfully delivered real payloads ('hello') on all three permitted ports (exit=0) while port 2222 timed out (exit=1) and reverse-direction traffic (node3->node2) also timed out, directly demonstrating both the permit and default-deny behavior.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-4a919d7cf0d7496a`, `cmd-66d5df9eeca54810`, `cmd-062a1b5e977c4ffa`, `cmd-5a31ad78c0d948fa`
- **req-4 — Satisfied:** Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1, node2, node3 with recovered service/config/connectivity state
  - **Why:** For all three nodes, distinct healthy-baseline boot identities were captured (node2 boot_id bdd5de93..., node3 boot_id 28ae5f98..., node1 kern.boottime Jun 14 2026), a restart was issued and acknowledged (connection reset/timeout observed), and a different post-restart boot identity was captured for each (node2 89d3a3b4..., node3 ee9dc003..., node1 kern.boottime Sep 5 17:51:12 2026) matching the fixed after-executor snapshot values. Post-restart state was independently re-verified: IP addressing/routes on node2 and node3, and on node1 the vtnet1/vtnet2 addresses, ip.forwarding=1, all three pf pass rules, and a live end-to-end TCP test on all three ports succeeding again — establishing the full pre/disruption/post recovery transition.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-bbfd7560217a493d`, `cmd-cd43d699a6364923`, `cmd-b0eedfa0658f4d02`, `cmd-5e5e9f0c9b7d4e9e`, `cmd-f418626690ec4298`, `cmd-539f2a7f13d84733`, `cmd-bf166e2b6f96477e`, `cmd-2a91d943bc044aa8`, `cmd-287223e3f08e4289`, `cmd-0d246754cd15476b`, `cmd-84009a97c905455a`, `cmd-7071b603077b4508`, `cmd-035ee5456c1d4595`, `cmd-7cf86bd6957142e8`, `cmd-6ad4a6ad1e4b46a2`, `cmd-69e5c406885b4a18`, `cmd-00b9e7c528fb4f8b`, `cmd-6853d1ebcb184746`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.880**. Executor mutations were bounded and largely served the task or the restart protocol. Config-editing scripts (/tmp/add_ifaces.py, /tmp/add_alias_rule.py) and their auto-created backups (config.xml.bak_ifaces, config.xml.bak_alias) were left on node1's filesystem rather than being cleaned up (cmd-15219ac0cecd4238, cmd-b15944886e42428f); these are low-risk residue (helper scripts and a safety backup of the edited config) but were not removed. Temporary nc listeners used for connectivity testing on node3 were explicitly torn down after each test round (cmd-1f24b68ebfb747a2, cmd-6853d1ebcb184746), leaving no lingering service state, though the second round's log files (nc8080b.log etc.) remained in /tmp per the after-executor snapshot. No failed services, no unsafe exposure, no destructive or unbounded actions were observed; all mutations trace clearly to satisfying the alias/rule requirement, the routing requirement, or the mandated restart protocol.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-15219ac0cecd4238`, `cmd-b15944886e42428f`, `cmd-1f24b68ebfb747a2`, `cmd-6853d1ebcb184746`, `global:after_executor:node1:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node3:temporary-files`
